I am an Associate Professor in the Department of Geography and the Environment at Villanova University, where I also direct the Environmental Studies Program. My lab studies spatial patterns in social-ecological systems and urban sustainability. Using spatial analysis, GIS and remote sensing, I investigate how urban environmental and ecological processes relate to the built environment, with active work on urban heat, air quality, flooding, green stormwater infrastructure, and equitable access to green space in Philadelphia and other US cities.

I am Co-PI on two NSF awards (SCC-IRG and DISES), PI of a William Penn Foundation grant supporting the Philadelphia Garden Data Collaborative, Associate Editor of *Sustainable Cities and Society*, and recipient of the 2023 Villanova Outstanding Faculty Mentor Award. I teach undergraduate and graduate courses in Geographic Information Systems, urban sustainability and the built environment, and have mentored dozens of graduate and undergraduate researchers.

I hold a PhD in Energy and Environmental Policy from the University of Delaware.

## Short bio

For introductions and programs. Peleg Kremer is an Associate Professor of Geography and the Environment at Villanova University and Director of its Environmental Studies Program. Her research uses spatial analysis, GIS and remote sensing to study how urban structure shapes environmental processes and their distribution across cities, with current projects on urban heat, flooding, green stormwater infrastructure and community gardens in Philadelphia. She is Co-PI on two NSF awards, leads the data work of the Philadelphia Garden Data Collaborative, and is Associate Editor of *Sustainable Cities and Society*. She holds a PhD in Energy and Environmental Policy from the University of Delaware.
